newsitem.title: USA: Florida home resales dip slightly in September.
newsitem.headline: Florida home resales dip slightly in September.

text.p: Florida sales of existing single-family homes declined by one percent in September, compared to the same month last year, the Florida Association of Realtors said Friday.
For the year to date however, home resales neared the 100,000 mark, besting last year's nine-month tally by 8 percent, the Realtors said.
The median sale price rose to $93,300 in September, an increase of 5 percent over last September.

Presidential election-year caution, rather than the slight upward drift in interest rates, was to blame for the September dip in resales, said Jack Meeks, president of Real Estate Professionals of America in Orlando.

"Investors we're being exposed constantly to campaign charges that the economy would suffer if one Presidential candidate or the other were elected," Meek said. "As a result, less sophisticated investors took a wait-and-see posture. But the marketplace is healthy and interest rates are reasonable."
The average rate of a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 8.23 percent in September 1996, compared to 7.64 percent in September 1995 and 8 percent in August 1996.
